title: EIF project-instance configuration (.eif/config.yaml) - user/project-owned
description: Mirrors .eif/config.yaml.example - keep both in sync. Validated by scripts/eif_validate_frontmatter.py --config. This file holds DESIRED, user-owned settings only - it is written once by eif_init and never overwritten by a routine upgrade. EIF-managed provenance (exact framework ref, bundle manifest, generated adapter entrypoint) lives in the separate, fully-regenerated framework-lock.schema.json / .eif/framework.lock.yaml - see docs/architecture/instance-contract.md for why the two are split.

schema_version.description: This config file's own schema version.

framework.description: Optional DESIRED framework release line - not provenance. Which framework commit actually generated this instance is recorded in .eif/framework.lock.yaml, not here.

adapter.description: User's declared adapter choice. `name` is deliberately NOT an enum here - the registry (scripts/eif_adapters.py) is the single source of truth for valid names, enforced by eif_init.py's argparse choices and cross-checked at runtime by eif_verify_runtime.py; duplicating the list in this schema would let the two drift silently. The generated entrypoint file and verified-version evidence are managed provenance - see .eif/framework.lock.yaml.

knowledge.description: Where this project's knowledge artifacts live. Greenfield default is root knowledge/ + knowledge/index.md - an existing-repository adoption can point these at wherever knowledge already lives (e.g. docs/knowledge/) instead of migrating content to match EIF's default. Generated instructions, eif_generate_index.py, and eif_search_knowledge.py invocations all read these values from config - they must not hardcode 'knowledge' independently of it.

root.description: Instance-relative path to the directory eif_generate_index.py scans and eif_search_knowledge.py searches. Default on a new instance: 'knowledge'.

index_path.description: Instance-relative path to the generated index file. Default on a new instance: '<root>/index.md'.

adoption.description: User-owned adoption/coexistence policy - deliberately NOT part of framework.lock.yaml (which is EIF-managed provenance): whether EIF coexists with pre-existing project governance is a project decision, not something EIF should infer or silently overwrite. migration_status in the lock records history (was this project greenfield or already-existing when first adopted); this section controls current behavior (how the generated block presents itself).

mode.description: greenfield: EIF-managed block may present itself as this project's baseline authority (default when eif_init finds no pre-existing entrypoint content). coexist: the generated block must not declare itself sole/primary authority, must not override pre-existing governance, and must state that project-owned instructions outside the markers stay canonical. Required to be set explicitly (via --adoption-mode) when eif_init's adoption preflight detects pre-existing entrypoint content - see scripts/eif_preflight.py.

suppressions.description: Controlled, auditable exceptions to scripts/eif_privacy_scan.py findings. Never weakens a detection pattern globally - each entry narrowly suppresses one rule at one path/glob, with a required rationale and review date. A suppression that no longer matches any real finding, or whose expires date has passed, is itself reported as a finding by the scanner (suppression hygiene) - it does not just silently keep working.

path.description: Exact repo-relative file path, or a narrow glob (fnmatch syntax). Deliberately not a directory-wide wildcard by convention - keep it as narrow as the actual reviewed case.

rationale.description: Why this specific finding is not a real issue - human-authored, reviewed text, never the matched secret value itself.

reviewed.description: ISO date this suppression was last reviewed by a human.

expires.description: Optional ISO date after which this suppression no longer applies (the finding reactivates and a suppression-hygiene finding fires). Omit for no automatic expiry.
